forest.name: A STAND OF FOREST
forest.what: THREE trees of different sizes standing apart, with clear sky between their canopies. Each tree is ONE straight bare trunk carrying ONE canopy, and that canopy is a single COMPACT ROUNDED MASS — a ball of foliage sitting on its trunk, closed and solid at its edge. Not a spreading crown, not several branches each with its own clump of leaves, not an open umbrella: a simple round head. The trunk is visible from the ground up to where the canopy begins, and it does not fork below that. Two or three small ferns at the roots and nothing else

forest_exhausted.name: A FELLED STAND OF FOREST
forest_exhausted.what: the SAME three trees after they have been felled: three low pale stumps with clean-cut tops, standing apart in the same arrangement, one cut log lying beside them, a scatter of woodchips and one small surviving sapling. It must read as the same place, logged — not as a different patch of ground

mountain.name: A ROCKY PEAK
mountain.what: ONE grey stone peak, cut into a few broad flat facets — six or seven large planes, not a pile of rubble. Its outline is craggy and uneven, leaning slightly, with one shoulder lower than the other. Two small boulders sit apart from it at its foot, and a little grass and moss catches in the lower cracks. It is a landmark on a single tile, not a mountain range

mountain_exhausted.name: A QUARRIED PEAK
mountain_exhausted.what: the SAME grey peak after it has been worked: its near side cut away into three or four flat stepped benches of pale freshly-cut stone, the rest of the outline still craggy, loose rubble and two squared blocks at its foot. Same rock, same place, mined into

mountain_iron.name: AN IRON PEAK
mountain_iron.what: ONE grey stone peak of a few broad flat facets, its outline craggy and uneven, shot through with rusty red-brown ore: two or three bold warm reddish veins running down its faces and one exposed nugget of dark iron, with a little rust-stained rubble at its foot. It must read as iron at a glance without any label, and the veins must be few and large enough to see at thumbnail size

mountain_iron_exhausted.name: A WORKED-OUT IRON PEAK
mountain_iron_exhausted.what: the SAME iron peak after it has been mined: one dark opening cut into its face with two rough timber props framing it, pale cut rock around the mouth, the red veins gone and only a little rust staining left, rubble at its foot

mountain_gold.name: A GOLD PEAK
mountain_gold.what: ONE grey stone peak of a few broad flat facets, its outline craggy and uneven, with bright gold veins running through it: two or three bold seams and one glinting nugget caught in a face, a little pale rubble at its foot. It must read as gold at a glance without any label, and the veins must be few and large enough to see at thumbnail size

mountain_gold_exhausted.name: A WORKED-OUT GOLD PEAK
mountain_gold_exhausted.what: the SAME gold peak after it has been mined: one dark opening cut into its face with two rough timber props framing it, pale cut rock around the mouth, the gold veins gone and only the faintest glint left, rubble at its foot

berry_bush.name: A BERRY BUSH
berry_bush.what: two rounded shrubs of dense dark-green leaves, thick with small bright berries — deep blue and red — with a few berries fallen at their feet. Plump and inviting; the bushes are low, well under the height of a person

wild_animals.name: WILD GAME
wild_animals.what: two or three wild boar standing on the ground, brown and bristly, compact and rounded in the game's style, with small tusks and alert ears. A few tufts of grass around their feet. They are gameplay-scale animals, not a portrait: calm, side-on, going about their business

fish_shoal.name: A FISH SHOAL
fish_shoal.what: a shoal of small silver-blue fish just under the surface of clear water, their shapes softened by the water above them, with a ring of gentle ripples and a few bubbles breaking the surface over them. NO water tile underneath — only the ripples and the fish themselves, as they will be laid over the game's own water

landmark_shrine.name: A WAYSIDE SHRINE
landmark_shrine.what: a small open stone shrine: four slim cream pillars carrying a little blue-tiled roof over a carved altar stone, two steps up to it, a blue-and-gold pennant on one pillar and a low ring of flowers around its base. Sacred and cared-for, and small — it seats nobody

landmark_stones.name: A RING OF STANDING STONES
landmark_stones.what: NINE weathered grey monoliths set in a wide ring, each tall, narrow and slightly leaning, pale lichen on their shoulders, two fallen flat across the circle. Short grass inside the ring. Ancient and plain — no carvings, no glow. The ring is wide enough to walk into

landmark_leyspring.name: A LEYSPRING
landmark_leyspring.what: a small pool of impossibly clear water welling up between pale rocks, lit from within with a soft cyan glow, faint motes of light rising off its surface and a delicate rim of frost-white crystal growing around its edge. Magical but quiet — no beam, no explosion

ruin_barrow.name: A BURIAL BARROW
ruin_barrow.what: a low grassy mound with a dark stone doorway broken open in its side, two leaning standing stones flanking the entrance and a slab fallen across the threshold. Long grass over the mound, a cold dark opening. Old, quiet and unwelcoming

ruin_chapel.name: A SUNKEN CHAPEL
ruin_chapel.what: The broken shell of a stone chapel, large enough to have been a parish church: one gable wall still standing with an empty arched window, a stub of square tower at one end, a long run of low broken wall marking the nave, the roof gone and charred beams fallen inside. Ivy over the stones and dark water pooled where the floor was

ruin_counting_house.name: A RUINED COUNTING HOUSE
ruin_counting_house.what: The burnt-out shell of a merchant's stone hall: two storeys of cracked cream wall with empty windows, the roof gone and charred beams fallen inside, a broken strongbox and spilled coins among the rubble at its foot, a torn awning still hanging from one wall

ruin_ironworks.name: DROWNED IRONWORKS
ruin_ironworks.what: The wreck of a forge: a cracked stone chimney stack still standing, a collapsed timber roof beside it, a rusted waterwheel half off its axle, and dark still water flooding the floor around broken anvils. Wide and low, sprawling across its ground rather than rising

ruin_observatory.name: A STAR OBSERVATORY IN RUINS
ruin_observatory.what: A broken round stone tower with its domed roof split open and half fallen away, a bent brass telescope tilting out through the gap, cracked steps spiralling up the outside, and a skirt of scattered stone rubble around its base. A trace of old blue paint left on the dome

farmlands.name: RIPE WHEAT
farmlands.what: Tall ripe wheat in warm golden straw and honey tones, grown in neat rows that run across the plot, the heads full and heavy and all at about the same height — waist-high on a person. A thin lip of dark tilled earth shows along the two near edges of the diamond, with the bottoms of the stalks visible against it

farmlands_exhausted.name: A HARVESTED FIELD
farmlands_exhausted.what: Bare warm-brown tilled earth in soft parallel ridges running across the plot, with short pale stubble left standing in the rows — ankle-high, nothing more — and a little loose straw caught between them. The same thin lip of dark earth along the two near edges of the diamond. It must read as the SAME field as the ripe one, cut

forest_2.name: A SMALL STAND OF TREES
forest_2.what: TWO trees, one taller than the other, standing a little apart with clear sky between their canopies. Each tree is ONE straight bare trunk carrying ONE canopy, and that canopy is a single COMPACT ROUNDED MASS — a ball of foliage sitting on its trunk, closed and solid at its edge. Not a spreading crown, not several branches each with its own clump of leaves, not an open umbrella: a simple round head. The trunk is visible from the ground up to where the canopy begins, and it does not fork below that. One small fern at the roots and nothing else

forest_3.name: A SMALL STAND OF TREES
forest_3.what: THREE trees of similar size in a loose triangle, one set back behind the other two, with clear sky between their canopies. Each tree is ONE straight bare trunk carrying ONE canopy, and that canopy is a single COMPACT ROUNDED MASS — a ball of foliage sitting on its trunk, closed and solid at its edge. Not a spreading crown, not several branches each with its own clump of leaves, not an open umbrella: a simple round head. The trunk is visible from the ground up to where the canopy begins, and it does not fork below that. A low bush at the foot of one of them and nothing else

mountain_2x2.name: A ROCKY MASSIF
mountain_2x2.what: ONE stone massif with TWO peaks of different heights sharing a base — the taller one behind and to the left, the lower one forward and right, with a saddle between them. Cut into broad flat facets, eight or ten large planes across the whole thing, not a heap of boulders. Its outline is craggy and uneven on every side, and it leans a little rather than standing square. Three or four small boulders at its foot and a little moss in the lower cracks

mountain_3x3.name: A MOUNTAIN RANGE ON ONE PLOT
mountain_3x3.what: ONE great stone massif with THREE peaks of clearly different heights sharing a base — the tallest at the back, two lower shoulders stepping down in front of it, saddles between them. Cut into broad flat facets, a dozen or so large planes, not a heap of boulders. Its outline is craggy and uneven on every side, and it leans a little rather than standing square. A scatter of boulders at its foot and moss in the lower cracks

mountain_exhausted_2x2.name: A QUARRIED MASSIF
mountain_exhausted_2x2.what: the SAME two-peaked massif after it has been worked: its near flank cut away into four or five flat stepped benches of pale freshly-cut stone, the peaks behind still craggy, loose rubble and two squared blocks at its foot. Same rock, same place, mined into

mountain_exhausted_3x3.name: A QUARRIED RANGE
mountain_exhausted_3x3.what: the SAME three-peaked massif after it has been worked: a wide terrace of flat stepped benches cut into its near flank in pale freshly-cut stone, the peaks behind still craggy, rubble and several squared blocks at its foot. Same rock, same place, mined into
